text:
eve_support: FYI incoming escalation from Dave at AcmeCorp — private deployment started seeing 502s and TLS handshake failures to the private control plane after a DC router firmware push earlier today. he attached a couple of curl/openssl traces.

dave_customer: we updated the edge router (vendor: XR-5400) at 03:20Z. afterwards our apps get 502 from the private endpoint and some services report TLS verify failures: 

  curl -v https://private.redwood.acme:443/api/health
    * TCP connection to private.redwood.acme port 443 failed: Connection reset
    * Closing connection 0
    curl: (56) TCP connection reset by peer

  openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme:443 -servername private.redwood.acme
    CONNECTED(00000003)
    140736....: TLS alert read: Fatal: handshake failure

eve_support: customer says access via their management VPN (not via DX) works fine; this only on the DX/VPC peering path. they already opened a TAC with vendor. want our help to confirm on our side and suggest mitigation.

ben_neteng: can you paste the traceroute and BGP session status from their DX router? also need the peering VLAN/ACLs and whether they have any TLS inspection / SNI rewrite enabled on the edge.

carol_sre: quick hypothesis: some hardware firewall/inspection device on their side is doing SNI-based interception and failing to forward the SNI header intact, or rewriting it, causing our cert selection to not match -> handshake fail. could also be an accidental egress allowlist blocking OCSP/CRL checks for cert chain.

ocsp-bot: automated check: our private endpoint (10.203.12.45:443) responded with full cert chain and OCSP stapling OK from eu-west-1 vantage. OCSP fetch to acme-responder.redwood-sec returns 200.

ben_neteng: dave, can you run these from a host behind the DX path (not the mgmt VPN) and paste results?
  1) curl --resolve private.redwood.acme:443:10.203.12.45 -v https://private.redwood.acme/
  2) openssl s_client -connect 10.203.12.45:443 -servername private.redwood.acme -status
  3) tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap (30s)

dave_customer: running now. curl gives: 
  * Connected to private.redwood.acme (10.203.12.45) port 443 (#0)
  * ALPN, offering http/1.1
  * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS header, CertificateRequest
  * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, description = certificate unknown
  * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, description = certificate unknown
  curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca

carol_sre: that error smells like SNI -> cert selection mismatch or an interceptor presenting a different cert signed by an internal CA that the client doesn't trust. Do you have a corporate TLS proxy?

dave_customer: we do have a downstream DPI box that does TLS inspection on customer egress per policy. after the router upgrade they said they pushed a new policy.

ben_neteng: OK. two prongs: 1) confirm whether the DPI/proxy is terminating TLS and re-issuing certs (client->proxy->server) vs passthrough. 2) if passthrough, check whether SNI is being stripped or truncated en route causing our server to present the wrong certificate for the connection IP.

carol_sre: can you export the first 1k of the tcpdump pcap (or paste the s_client -status output)? specifically need to see ClientHello SNI extension raw. run: 
  tcpdump -nn -A -s 0 'tcp port 443 and (tcp[32] != 0)' -c 200

dave_customer: attached base64 of the pcap head (pasted inline). they also ran s_client -status and got: 
  OCSP response: no response sent
  Certificate chain
  1 s:/CN=private.redwood.acme
  ...
  verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate

eve_support: ocsp-bot already confirmed our endpoint staples OCSP. this matches the idea that the client sees a different cert chain (proxy CA).

ben_neteng: can you get the proxy to bypass inspection for traffic to 10.203.12.45 (or for SNI private.redwood.acme) as a quick mitigation? most proxies support an allowlist/ passthrough for specific FQDNs or IPs.

dave_customer: customer tried a bypass for the IP and still saw resets. vendor says bypass rules were applied but the firewall also enforces an MTU clamp and deep packet normalization that may restart TLS flows.

carol_sre: another angle: if normalization is modifying TLS record sizes or removing TLS extensions (SNI, status_request), some clients will abort with handshake failure. please confirm if there are any middleboxes doing TLS record coalescing, tcp splitting, or SNI rewrite.

dave_customer: asking TAC to check DPI policy. vendor replies they see three TLS flows where the proxy presents a placeholder cert (CN=internal-proxy) and OCSP is not stapled. they flagged a signature mismatch.

ben_neteng: confirmed on our side we see the TCP connection from their DX virtual interface but the TLS handshake completes only when the client uses the mgmt VPN path. traceroute shows same AS path but different next-hop devices. so this is definitely their perimeter device.

carol_sre: mitigation suggestions to give the customer: 
  - Add an explicit passthrough rule for private.redwood.acme and the endpoint IP (10.203.12.45) on the DPI/proxy.
  - Allow OCSP/CRL egress to our CA responder endpoints: ocsp.redwood-sec.example (TCP/HTTP 80/443) and CRL fetch URLs.
  - Disable SNI-based interception for this destination.
  - If passthrough not possible: configure mutual TLS (mTLS) on the private endpoint so the proxy cannot silently MITM without presenting client certs (requires rollout coordination).
  - As a short-term workaround, route their inference traffic over the mgmt VPN while TAC fixes the DX path.

dave_customer: TAC applied passthrough for the FQDN and allowed ocsp egress; after a ~60s jitter the traffic started flowing again. their apps report healthy. they left the DPI in passthrough for now.

eve_support: closing loop: customer asked for a short runbook to prevent regressions: 
  - record DPI policy change window and require canary on a subset of hosts
  - add monitoring for TLS handshake failure rate (5xx/502 + openssl alerts) on private routes
  - ensure ocsp/CRL egress allowlist is in config templates for DX peering stacks

carol_sre: I'll open a KB with the runbook and recommended firewall rules + sample tcpdump/openssl commands. tagging ben_neteng for the routing/network notes.

ben_neteng: noted. also suggested adding an active probe from the DX path that validates SNI and OCSP stapling every 5m.

dave_customer: thanks everyone, TAC will close after change window. appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

eve_support: marking resolved for now. will follow up if they revert passthrough and see problems. :white_check_mark:
